    Cited inputs on bricks over string and gentle algebras #

    • isString_of_isBrick: over a brick-finite string algebra, every brick is a string module (Butler–Ringel's string–band classification, Theorem 4.5, with the exclusion of band bricks recalled before Proposition 5.2).
    • isRepFinite_of_isBrickFinite: Lemma 5.1, a brick-finite gentle algebra is representation-finite (Plamondon's band bricks, proved in Classification.Plamondon).
    source
    theorem BrickAccessibility.isString_of_isBrick {k : Type u} [Field k] {B : Type u} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] [IsAlgClosed k] [FiniteDimensional k B] (D : MonomialData k B) (hD : D.IsStringAlgebra) (hbf : IsBrickFinite B) (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module k M] [IsScalarTower k B M] [FiniteDimensional k M] (hM : IsBrick B M) :
    ∃ (w : Word D.Q) (hw : Word.IsString D w), Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[B] Word.stringModule D w hw)

    Over a brick-finite string algebra over an algebraically closed field, every finite-dimensional brick is isomorphic to a string module.

    Lemma 5.1. A brick-finite gentle algebra over an algebraically closed field is representation-finite.
